Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC Enters Insolvency, Mining Operations Disrupted Across Kyrgyzstan

BISHKEK, June 7—Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC, one of Kyrgyzstan’s largest metals and mining companies, has entered insolvency proceedings, causing immediate disruptions to its mining and refining activities nationwide, company officials said Friday.

The insolvency process, which began earlier this week, has already led to the suspension of operations at several major sites, including the flagship gold ore processing plant in the Jalal-Abad region. Dozens of workers were seen leaving the facility Friday morning as company representatives briefed staff on the situation.

"Today we had to halt production at our main facility due to the uncertainty around the company’s finances," said Azamat Kadyrov, Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC’s acting director, at a press conference in Bishkek. "We are working closely with the administrators and government bodies to seek a resolution, but at this stage, we cannot confirm when or if operations will resume."

Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC is a key employer in the country’s mining sector and a major contributor to the national budget. According to figures from the Kyrgyz Mining Association, the company accounted for nearly 18% of Kyrgyzstan’s gold output last year. Its insolvency has raised concerns among local communities and industry analysts about supply chains and employment stability.

“We are deeply worried about the future of our jobs and our families,” said Ruslan Akmatov, a union representative at the Toktogul mine. “There are more than 3,000 workers who depend on these wages.”

The State Agency for Geology and Mineral Resources said it was monitoring the situation closely and would provide support to affected workers and local governments. “The insolvency of Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC is a matter of national significance,” an agency spokesperson told reporters, adding that efforts were underway to maintain site safety and environmental controls during the period of uncertainty.

Industry analysts say the insolvency may prompt a broader review of financial practices and regulatory oversight in Kyrgyzstan’s mining sector. For now, the administration process at Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC is ongoing, with no timeline yet established for a potential restructuring, sale of assets, or liquidation.
